details: CONFIRMED by probe. `git patch-id --stable` strips all whitespace before hashing (git docs: "with whitespace and line numbers
ignored"); `--verbatim` keeps it (and cannot be combined with --stable; it implies a stable id). With the default mode the two
patches above hash to the same id c5a54cfd..., with --verbatim to 934a7aef... and adc04abb.... The owner's item defines "unchanged"
as range-diff showing no change; range-diff does show this change. Indentation is semantics in Python and YAML, relay's own
languages, so a behaviour change lands under an old check; only the gate stands between it and the merge.
Size: 15 minutes (one flag and one test).
evidence: bash scratchpad/probe/ws.sh (repo with the two versions above)
git diff master HEAD | git patch-id --stable      -> c5a54cfd637589a282c4a454a2d69c3f043bf929
git diff master <old> | git patch-id --stable     -> c5a54cfd637589a282c4a454a2d69c3f043bf929
git range-diff old~1..old master..wt/x            -> 1: fabb5f9 ! 1: 7b9de6c change ... -+    h()  ++        h()
git patch-id --verbatim on each                   -> 934a7aef... vs adc04abb... (different)
failing_case: Branch wt/x adds to lib_x.py:
if a:
A check mark and a review are recorded on that commit (old). The commit is then amended (or rebased with a conflict edit) so h() is
indented under the if (a behaviour change in Python). `git range-diff` shows `1: fabb5f9 ! 1: 7b9de6c change` (a changed patch).
relay_inert.twin(repo, old, "refs/heads/wt/x") now returns the new commit 7b9de6c..., so relay_marks.marks() carries the old mark to
it and _review_findings accepts the old review: the merge hook takes a check of code nobody checked. It should return None (records
voided), as the item promises: "a rebase that changes the patch still voids them".
fix_hint: In _patch_id use ["git", "-C", repo, "patch-id", "--verbatim"] instead of "--stable"; add a RebasedRecords test that re-indents a
line after the mark and asserts marks() does not carry it and _review_findings refuses.
pass_cases: 1. Whitespace-only change of indentation in a .py line of the branch's patch after the review: twin(old) is None;
_review_findings raises VerdictError "not in the history"; marks() holds no entry for the new head; step_mark refuses.
2. Rebase onto a default-branch commit that touches an unrelated file, patch byte-identical: twin returns the rebased commit (as
test_a_review_of_a_commit_a_clean_rebase_replaced_still_counts today).
3. Rebase whose patch changes content (x = 1 -> x = 2): twin is None (as the existing changed-patch tests).
4. A trailing-space-only change on a branch line: twin is None (the patch changed; range-diff shows `!`).
reason: tests/test_verdict.py:679-709 re-indent and trailing-space tests pass; fail at b6961152.
findings.summary: git patch-id ignores whitespace, so a rebase or amend that only re-indents code (a changed Python patch) keeps the old review and check

details: CONFIRMED by probe (scratchpad/probe/same.sh): twin -> 0e36c75..., relay_inert.changed(old, head, own=True) -> ['lib_x.py'].
Mechanism: relay's design (merge hook step_mark and the M findings of build_findings) holds that when the default branch changes a
file the branch also changed, the combined file is checked again, even when git merged it cleanly. git's patch id hashes only the
branch's own hunks with line numbers dropped, so a default-branch edit outside the hunks' 3 context lines leaves the patch id the
same. The item says "git range-diff shows no change" keeps the records, which this case satisfies, so the item and the merge rule
disagree; only the owner can pick. Answer (a) is the item as written; (b) costs one more relay_inert.changed call per twin and
loses the saving for rebases over shared files (not measured how often arsenal's Master Sync hits a shared file).
Size: 15 minutes for (b), 5 for (a).
evidence: git range-diff old~1..old master..wt/x   -> 1:  e383d7b = 1:  0e36c75 branch
failing_case: lib_x.py has lines x1..x30. Branch wt/x changes x3 and is checked (mark on old). The default branch then changes x28 of the same
file. Taken by a merge commit, the merge hook refuses ("after the check of <old>, wt/x changed lib_x.py") and the next check gets an
M finding for lib_x.py. Taken by a rebase, range-diff shows `1: e383d7b = 1: 0e36c75 branch`, twin() returns the rebased commit and
the old mark is accepted: the combined lib_x.py, which no checker read, merges with only a gate.
fix_hint: For (b): in twin(), after finding the candidate, return it only when changed(repo, old, candidate, own=True) is empty.
pass_cases: Depends on the owner's answer:
a) Keep the item's rule (range-diff "=" keeps the records): the case above keeps the mark; documented in the item's design note.
b) Match the merge rule: twin() also requires that no own file of the old patch differs between the old and new merge-base
(relay_inert.changed(old, twin, own=True) is empty); the case above then yields no twin and step_mark refuses, while the
unrelated-file rebase (test_a_review_of_a_commit_a_clean_rebase_replaced_still_counts) still keeps the records.
reason: Owner said a (keep records on range-diff equal) but the fix implements b (lib/relay_inert.py twin returns None when own files changed). Test passes, but it contradicts the owner decision. Owner entry present.
findings.summary: a rebase over a default-branch change to one of the branch's own files keeps the check, where the same change by merge needs a new check (M finding)

failing_case: lib/relay_marks.py:200 `def rebased(repo, ref, have):` is a new function with no types; marks() (189), show() (300) and
relay_verdict._review_findings (631) changed and stay untyped. The project rule "Every new or changed function has types" is not met.
fix_hint: Annotate the four functions; mirror into plugins/relay/lib and plugins/front/lib copies.
pass_cases: 1. rebased(repo: str, ref: str, have: set[str]) -> list[tuple[str, dict]] (or the mark's typed record).
2. marks, show and _review_findings carry parameter and return types; the type checker the gate runs stays green.
reason: Types added to marks, rebased, show, _review_findings; the types-and-lint step of precheck is ok.

details: PLAUSIBLE (git docs: git diff uses diff.external and textconv unless --no-ext-diff / --no-textconv). Not probed. Size: 5 minutes.
failing_case: A repository with diff.external set (or a textconv driver on a file type): `git diff` prints the external tool's output or the
converted text, not the patch. With diff.external, the output is not a patch, patch-id prints nothing and every twin is None (the
feature silently off); with textconv, two different binaries whose converted text is equal give one patch id (a false twin).
fix_hint: Add "--no-ext-diff", "--no-textconv", "--no-color" to the git diff call (or use git diff-tree -p).
pass_cases: 1. With `git config diff.external /bin/true` in the test repo, a clean rebase still keeps the records.
2. Without that config, results are unchanged.
reason: diff.external test passes and fails at b6961152; flags --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-color are in _patch_id.
findings.summary: _patch_id runs porcelain `git diff`, which honours the user's diff.external and textconv drivers
